assertions.name: mirror_split_proportional_to_canonical_coulomb_all_A
assertions.source: split_AME/ΔE_C(canonical Z(Z−1), R=λ̄_π·A^{1/3}) = 0.975 ± 0.089 (9% spread) across 8 mirror pairs A=3–39 ⇒ the split is proportional to Coulomb ⇒ the strong kernel must be charge-symmetric. The spread is a monotone TREND, not constant scatter (Pearson r = 0.824); the proportionality conclusion is unaffected.

assertions.name: mirror_ratio_trends_monotonically_with_A
assertions.source: Pearson r = 0.824 between split/ΔE_C and A over the 8 pairs; t = 3.57 on 6 dof exceeds the 2.447 two-sided p=0.05 critical value, and a straight line has rms 0.0502 against the mean's 0.0887. Recorded so 'ratio_mean' is not consumed as if it applied at every A — at A=3 the ratio is 0.806.

description: The mirror binding split is Coulomb across the isobaric chain ³H/³He…³⁹K/³⁹Ca: using the repo's canonical uniform-sphere Coulomb (Z(Z−1) self-energy, R = λ̄_π·A^{1/3} with λ̄_π = ℏc/m_π the CAL-3 length, coulomb_energy.mirror_displacement_mev; no continuous fitted parameter, but the coefficient 1 on λ̄_π is a SELECTION and A^{1/3} an ASSUMPTION, see docs/audits/2026-07-13-pion-radius-and-vol-to-radius-gaps.md; label corrected 2026-11-27, it said r₀=1.2 fm, which this module stopped using on 2026-08-09), the ratio split_AME/ΔE_C = 0.97 ± 0.09 across A=3–39. ⇒ the split is proportional to Coulomb, so any QOU strong kernel must be charge-symmetric (Coulomb separate); the #2089 kernel's 2.27 MeV A=3 strong split (#3564) is 3× the whole observed split, systematically. Scope-(a), no wiring. ⚠ THE RATIO IS NOT CONSTANT (corrected 2026-08-25): this field said '≈constant across A=3–39'. It rises monotonically — Pearson r = 0.824, t = 3.57 on 6 dof (p < 0.05), and a line beats the mean by 43% in rms. The proportionality finding and the charge-symmetry consequence are unaffected; only the 'constant' characterisation was wrong. Consumers must say WHICH A: the A=3 (³H/³He) ratio is 0.806, not the chain mean 0.97.

ratio_trend_in_A.note: The ratio is NOT constant in A; it rises monotonically. A line describes the eight points better than their mean. Quote the A you need, not ratio_mean.
